questions.q: Why does the Order Count measure use DISTINCTCOUNT(FactProductSales[SalesOrderID]) instead of a plain COUNTROWS?
options: COUNTROWS only works on dimension tables, not fact tables
DISTINCTCOUNT is always faster than COUNTROWS regardless of grain
SalesOrderID cannot be used with COUNTROWS
dw.FactProductSales is at the order-line grain, so COUNTROWS would count line items, not distinct orders
questions.explain: Since the fact table has one row per order line, counting distinct SalesOrderID values is what actually answers 'how many orders' at the correct grain.

questions.q: Why does Average Order Value use DIVIDE instead of writing [Total Sales] / [Order Count] directly?
options: The / operator is not supported in Power BI at all
DIVIDE automatically formats the result as currency
DIVIDE is required syntax in every DAX measure
DIVIDE returns blank instead of throwing a divide-by-zero error when a slicer filters the data down to zero orders
questions.explain: A slicer combination with no matching orders would cause a plain division to error; DIVIDE handles that case gracefully by returning blank.

questions.q: What does ALL ( DimTerritory ) do inside the Total Sales (All Territories) measure?
options: It strips away any filter currently applied through the DimTerritory relationship, recalculating Total Sales as if the whole table were unfiltered
It sorts DimTerritory alphabetically before calculating
It returns the total number of rows in DimTerritory
It deletes the DimTerritory table from the model
questions.explain: ALL(DimTerritory) removes any slicer, visual, or drill-down filter currently applied through that table, giving a genuinely unfiltered company-wide total.

questions.q: With no territory filter applied anywhere on a report page, how do [Total Sales] and [Total Sales (All Territories)] compare?
options: Total Sales (All Territories) is always zero until a filter is applied
They always differ by exactly the discount percentage
They can never be compared in the same visual
They return the exact same number, since ALL has nothing to strip away when nothing is filtered in the first place
questions.explain: The two measures only diverge once an actual territory filter narrows the data down — with no filter, there's nothing for ALL to remove, so both return the same value.

questions.q: Why does the exact value of Total Sales (All Territories), evaluated unfiltered, matter beyond this chapter?
options: It is only used internally by Power BI and never shown to users
It has no significance outside of Chapter 4
It gets deleted once the Tableau deck is built
It's the real company-wide quarterly total this capstone later checks Finance's independently-built Excel total against in Chapter 7
questions.explain: This measure's unfiltered value is the Power BI quarterly total that Finance's Excel reconciliation and the Chapter 7 discrepancy investigation are built directly around.
